page_title: Current Proof | Encrypted Sensitive Record Sync
title: Encrypted sensitive records, provider-token lifecycle, and bounded background sync
summary: This repo now ships a narrow runtime proof slice for secure backend work: provider tokens and authorized payloads are stored encrypted with explicit key IDs, stub mode syncs deterministically by default, sandbox mode can run real outbound HTTPS when configured, and the live lab shows persisted sensitive-access grants, key-custody evidence, denied reads, and audited authorized access.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: The proof pivot needed visible evidence for encrypted-at-rest storage, token lifecycle handling, and integration-boundary discipline instead of only architectural groundwork.
The repo needed a bounded implementation slice that stayed honest about scope and avoided claiming real healthcare or real-provider integrations.
The public proof surface had to show guest-safe redaction, denied signed-in reads without grants, and audited authorized reads from the same stored records.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Added a new sensitive-data bounded context across domain, app, infra, and HTTP without splitting the repo into new crates.
Stored provider tokens and authorized record payloads with AES-256-GCM encryption, while keeping only redacted labels and last-four evidence queryable in cleartext.

Wired a two-mode provider boundary: deterministic local stub by default, plus an opt-in sandbox HTTP adapter with credential exchange, bounded retry/backoff state, cursor-based record sync, key-versioned ciphertext storage, persisted sensitive-access grants, and a live lab panel that exposes denied-vs-allowed reads with recent audit evidence.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: The repo now backs secure-systems claims with a running encrypted-storage, key-rotation, and background-sync slice instead of only narrative direction.
Reviewers can inspect operator-only token status, last sync state, redacted records, ciphertext evidence, key-custody state, denied reads, and audited authorized-read boundaries in the live app.

The implementation stays sanitized and bounded: deterministic stub mode for repeatable proof runs, an opt-in sandbox mode for real outbound HTTPS, explicit trust boundaries, and no overclaim about PHI or production vendor operations.

page_title: Supporting Proof | Automation at Fundraising Scale
title: Automated fundraiser acknowledgments to remove high-volume backlog
summary: This archived GoodUnited case study is supporting proof of execution under operational pressure. It covers replacing a manual thank-you workflow with browser automation that increased throughput and consistency.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: Manual thank-you workflows were time-consuming, error-prone, and perpetually behind demand.
Teams depended on queue dashboards and manual triage but still accumulated backlog.
Large nonprofit clients generated very high monthly fundraiser volume, making manual scaling expensive.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Built a Playwright + TypeScript automation worker to emulate the existing browser workflow end to end.
Encoded template selection and variable substitution logic to reduce operator variance and mistakes.
Scaled execution to 72 concurrent instances to keep pace with continuously arriving fundraiser pages.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: Delivered roughly 12x speed compared to a single manual operator for the same task shape.
Eliminated persistent backlog and reduced error rates in outbound fundraiser communication.
Faster response windows increased fundraiser engagement and improved downstream support effectiveness.

page_title: Supporting Proof | Realtime Fundraiser Data Pipeline
eyebrow: Supporting Proof Archive · Realtime Product Systems
title: Replaced delayed CSV workflows with realtime fundraiser + donation visibility
summary: This archived fundraiser pipeline is supporting proof of building under live integration pressure. It moved operations from delayed CSV snapshots to realtime creation and donation signals integrated with Meta APIs.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: Prior workflow depended on manually downloaded CSV files that were at least 48 hours delayed.
Teams could only see fundraisers after donations appeared, missing newly created but not-yet-donated pages.
The lag degraded outreach speed and reduced the ability to guide fundraisers effectively.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Built an Express + Svelte + MongoDB app for event participants to create fundraisers in one click.
Integrated Meta APIs so fundraiser creation events were captured at source instead of inferred later.
Surfaced donation activity in realtime, enabling chat and success teams to operate with current context.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: Eliminated 48-hour baseline delay in fundraiser discovery and donation context.
Enabled operations across millions of users and tens of millions of donation data points.
Improved decision quality across sales, customer success, and analytics functions.

page_title: Supporting Proof | Custom Substack Publishing Platform
title: Built a custom Substack publishing platform around a CMS event pipeline
summary: This archived Rust publishing platform is supporting proof of systems design under integration constraints. It ingests Directus CMS events, processes them through queued workers, and executes automated publishing flows through a custom Substack integration.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: Editorial and publishing workflows needed reliable automation across CMS content lifecycle events.
Substack operations required custom integration logic because official API support was limited for needed flows.
The system had to preserve determinism and observability across asynchronous event processing.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Built a custom Substack client/integration layer for publish-oriented automation paths.
Typed Directus webhook events by collection/operation and routed them into queue-backed processing.
Structured a 13-crate Rust workspace across libs, services, and tools to keep boundaries explicit.
Used Axum services and worker processing to run end-to-end automation chains from trigger to publish.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: Replaced manual handoff-heavy publishing work with deterministic event-driven automation.
Created a reusable platform foundation for additional CMS-triggered automation chains.
Established a clear hardening roadmap through architecture review of reliability and CI/security gaps.
